clue.text: Worker filling in, hired as a model

parts.note: a temp is a worker standing in for someone absent
let means rented out, hired

explanation.surface: A stand-in employee has been taken on as a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A templet is a variant spelling of template, a pattern or guide used as a model.

clue.text: Something partially fermented is returned — beer's not right

indicators.note: returned says the little word is is to be read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not right says the letter standing for right is dropped from the beer

parts.note: beer's here reads as beer is, with lager the beer
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A brewer complains that a half-fermented batch came back because the beer was off.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'beer's' stands for 'is', so the beer is without its R; 'returned' turns only the little word 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fodder kept in a silo, where it is preserved by partial fermentation.

clue.text: College wizard is entertaining a learner in study

indicators.note: entertaining as a host does means holding the next pieces inside the wizard

parts.note: a mage is a magician or wizard

indicators.note: in says the article and learner go inside the study

parts.note: a den is a private study or work room
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A college magician hosts a student in his study.
explanation.walkthrough: Magdalene College at Cambridge; 'is entertaining' and 'in' are two separate container signals, one nested in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalene is one of the colleges of Cambridge University.

clue.text: Sporting venue's no good? Not quite a description of the Oval!

definitions.text: Not quite a description of the Oval!

indicators.note: no here means the venue is without the letter for good

parts.note: a ground is a sports venue; 's reads as is

explanation.surface: A remark that a famous sports ground is no good, nor even properly circular.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground; an oval shape is close to circular but not quite, so the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is nearly circular, so this word describes it only approximately.

clue.text: Wig as Counsel's foremost disguise

indicators.note: foremost asks for the leading letter of the word Counsel's

parts.note: to hide is to conceal or disguise

explanation.surface: A barrister's wig serves as his main disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wig' looks like a barrister's headgear but is the verb meaning to scold, as in 'wigging'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wig someone, in old British slang, is to rebuke or scold them.

clue.text: Dog can repeatedly run home to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with places the run and home letters at the front of the answer

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
in means at home

indicators.note: repeatedly says the container word appears more than once

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A dog keeps running home to its can of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rin Tin Tin was a famous German Shepherd film star of Hollywood's silent era.

clue.text: Parker's characteristic as head admitting old shortcoming

indicators.note: admitting means letting the following pieces inside the headland

parts.note: a ness is a headland or head
a sin is a failing or shortcoming

explanation.surface: A school head confesses to a past failing as the defining trait of someone named Parker.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nosey Parker is a British term for a busybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosey parker's defining trait is prying curiosity into other people's business.

clue.text: Quiet tavern, extremely agreeable, The Feathers?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
an inn is a tavern

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of agreeable

explanation.surface: A peaceful pub called The Feathers is very pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Feathers sounds like a pub name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinnae are feathers or wings, also the leaflets of a compound leaf.

clue.text: Topped up? Not at first — time to provide liquid shortfall

indicators.note: Not at first says the opening letter of the filled-up word is dropped

parts.note: a glass topped up is full
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A barman fails to top up drinks at first and is then given time to make up the shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullage is the amount by which a container falls short of being full.

clue.text: Money needed to secure one or other being this?

definitions.text: Money needed to secure one or other being this?

parts.words: Money needed to secure one or other being this?
parts.note: a captive whose freedom is bought by payment of a sum is in this state

explanation.surface: A question of what someone is when cash is needed to secure them.
explanation.definitionFit: A person freed by payment of a demanded sum has been redeemed for money.

clue.text: Paint setting with time — not keen to watch it though?

definitions.text: not keen to watch it though?

indicators.note: setting, as paint hardens, signals the letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: Watching paint set takes time, and nobody wants to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' rearranges PAINT and TIME; the definition alludes to the boredom of watching paint dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone short of patience would dread watching paint dry, which is proverbially tedious.

clue.text: Ancient civilisation captured by the German artist from Nuremburg

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the German article

parts.note: der is German for the
Ur was the ancient Sumerian city-state

explanation.surface: An ancient civilisation was depicted by a German painter from Nuremberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer, the Renaissance painter and engraver, was born in Nuremberg.

clue.text: Creative powers in the first verse of the Bible?

definitions.meaning: plural of genius, an inborn creative gift

definitions.text: the first verse of the Bible?
definitions.meaning: Genesis chapter 1 verse 1 written as Gen i i

explanation.surface: Creative inspiration lies in the opening words of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis 1:1 is abbreviated Gen. i. i.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genius, meaning spirits or exceptional creative talents.

clue.text: Greek character borne by transport. Opposite of hair-raising experience?

indicators.note: borne by means carried inside the word for rapture

parts.note: transport in the sense of rapture or elation
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is carried by a vehicle, then a hair-raising experience is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like a vehicle but means rapture, ELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair removal is the reverse of raising hairs, playfully the opposite of hair-raising.

clue.text: Encourage newspaper to include something prophetic

indicators.note: to include means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
an omen foretells the future

explanation.surface: A request that a paper print a prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment is to stir up or incite trouble, hence to encourage it.

clue.text: Material from festival meal

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: Fabric taken from a festive dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Galatea is a strong striped cotton fabric, once used for children's clothes.

clue.text: What I'm experiencing is not suitable for those who are 22

definitions.text: What I'm experiencing is not suitable for those who are 22

parts.words: What I'm experiencing is not suitable for those who are 22
parts.note: read literally, the period eats up the word I'm, framing it; such long-winded tasks are wrong for people lacking patience

explanation.surface: A complaint that slow tasks are not for restless people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 answer is IMPATIENT; T and E of TIME literally enclose I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthy tasks that take ages suit nobody short of patience.

clue.text: Sucker wanting drink in cups

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the cups

parts.note: mugs are drinking cups
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A dupe wants gin served in cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is British slang for a fool or easy dupe, often oneself.

clue.text: Abandon holiday

definitions.meaning: to go away from or desert

explanation.definitionFit: To leave is to abandon; leave is also permitted time off work.

clue.text: Men taken in by sort of believer who might be looking for proof?

definitions.text: who might be looking for proof?
definitions.note: the definition is a relative clause standing for a person who seeks proof

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the believer

parts.note: a theist believes in God
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are converted by a believer who wants evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' as other ranks, ordinary soldiers, is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoretician proposes ideas that then need testing and proof.

clue.text: Capital city wants new leader to bring colour

indicators.note: wants new leader says the city's first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Vienna is the capital of Austria

explanation.surface: A capital city needs a fresh mayor to brighten it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The V of VIENNA is replaced by S; the clue does not say which letter, so crossings settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is a reddish-brown earth pigment, and the colour named after it.

clue.text: English poet's entertaining revolutionary Irish yobs

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: Philip Larkin was an English poet; the 's supplies the final letter

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning the abbreviation round

explanation.surface: An English poet hosts a rebellious Irishman among hooligans.
explanation.definitionFit: Larrikin is Australian slang for a rowdy hooligan or lout.

clue.text: One ultimately full in stomach that's put on much weight?

definitions.text: One ultimately full in stomach that's put on much weight?

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the stomach

parts.note: gut is the stomach

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the closing letter of full

parts.note: a ton is a large weight

explanation.surface: A person stuffed to the gills has gained a lot of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: An overeater ends up full in the belly and heavy.

clue.text: A learned don, I'd rewritten book

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A scholarly don has redrafted a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Deronda is George Eliot's last novel, published in 1876.

clue.text: Dark story containing fine entertainment

parts.note: night is darkness

indicators.note: containing means the story holds the next letter

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A grim tale includes a good show.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightlife means evening entertainment such as clubs, bars and shows.

clue.text: Move on board launch to get fish

parts.note: to cast is to throw or launch
ling is a long cod-like fish

explanation.surface: Throwing a line from a boat to land a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is a chess move in which king and rook shift together.

clue.text: One of the popes with long internal battle

indicators.note: internal means sitting inside the pope's name

parts.note: Leo is a name taken by many popes
to pant for is to long for

explanation.surface: A pope with an inner yearning fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto was the 1571 sea battle in which the Holy League beat the Ottoman fleet.

clue.text: Number turning up in market wanting redistribution of goods etc?

definitions.note: adjective use: a supporter of communist redistribution

indicators.note: in places the number inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the number reads upward, backwards

parts.note: six is a number

explanation.surface: Someone at a market calls for goods to be shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads a word bottom to top, so the number is written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Karl Marx seeks common ownership and fair sharing of wealth.

clue.text: Feel bitter about what tenant has to pay around Home Counties

indicators.note: around means the payment wraps the next piece

parts.note: rent is paid by a tenant
SE, south-east, is the region of the Home Counties around London

explanation.surface: A tenant feels bitter about rent in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties around London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel aggrieved or bitter about it.

clue.text: Slow speech to attract lover — but maiden maybe put off

parts.note: to draw is to attract

indicators.note: put off means the cricket term is removed from the lover

parts.note: taken as written
a maiden is one kind of over in cricket, one with no runs

explanation.surface: Drawling to attract a lover, though a young woman may be put off.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored; 'maiden' looks like a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lengthened manner of speaking.
